PREREGISTERED.quantity: DiD = mean(delta on ortholog_bearing) - mean(delta on withheld_orthology_free), delta = committed_CE - assessed_CE per window (positive = assessed better)

outcomes.LEAK_RESOLVED_AT_PREDICTED_SIZE: CI excludes zero AND contains the predicted -0.0054
outcomes.LEAK_RESOLVED_BUT_SMALLER_THAN_PREDICTED: CI excludes zero AND lies entirely between zero and the predicted size -- a real leak, smaller than the design expected
outcomes.LEAK_EXCLUDED_AT_PREDICTED_SIZE: CI contains zero AND excludes the predicted -0.0054 -- the predicted leak size is ruled out, which the 120-window run could not do
outcomes.STILL_UNRESOLVED: CI contains BOTH zero and the predicted size -- more windows did not settle it

PREREGISTERED.resolution_rule: a percentile bootstrap 95% CI, matching the committed scorer's convention
PREREGISTERED.why_this_is_not_a_relabelled_null: the 120-window interval contained both zero and the predicted size, so it distinguished nothing. An interval that contains zero while EXCLUDING -0.0054 is a different and stronger statement, and it is reachable only at larger n.

VERDICT.reading: CI contains zero AND excludes the predicted -0.0054 -- the predicted leak size is ruled out, which the 120-window run could not do

comparison_to_120_windows.note: a narrower interval is expected from n alone; the VERDICT, not the width, is what changed or did not

honest_limits: The DiD identifies the leak only if cross-organism cost acts equally on both halves and cancels. That is the design's assumption and is not testable from these numbers.
Scoped to this corpus and this checkpoint pair; not a general claim about leakage.
An interval excluding the predicted size says the prediction was wrong, NOT that the true value is the new centre.
The two halves are disjoint, so the DiD is a difference of independent means; the within-set delta is paired per window and that pairing is preserved.
